title: Frames end in because or so that
statement: A frame for using a taught word includes the word and ends in 'because' or 'so that', never a blank for the word or its definition.
detail: A grade-3 reading rulebook's vocabulary routine says open frames end in because or so that, and a reading quality canon applied in a grade-5 audit requires a sentence frame to contain the target word and stay open-ended, banning the closed anti-patterns 'admire means ___' and fill-the-blank-with-the-word. The same canon asks vocabulary checks to reach the generative level, such as completing an idea that ends in because, rather than associational matching. An open ending means the learner's answer has to give a reason, not just the word.
against: A different exercise keeps the closed form on purpose: the record practise-taught-words-by-typed-recall cues each taught word by its meaning in a one-blank sentence for typed recall, which practises recalling the word rather than using it.

evidence.quote: Open frames end in BECAUSE / SO THAT; contrast near-neighbours; never assess a word the turn you taught it; a glossary pop-up is never instruction; prefer generative words; never target a word the passage explains in place.
A sentence frame contains the target word and is open-ended (ends in 'because…/so that…'); ban the closed anti-patterns ('*admire* means ___' and fill-the-blank-with-the-word).

Vocabulary checks reach the generative level (idea-completion '…forbidden to play with matches because ___'; 'would you want a frail person on your team? why?'), not associational matching; classify items by cognitive demand.
